```yaml
# repo-map.yaml
#
# This is the only file every agent reads in full. Everything else in this
# repository is read on demand, through the slice defined for the part you
# were assigned.
#
# It answers exactly three questions:
#   1. What are the parts?             -> parts:
#   2. What depends on what?           -> parts.<id>.depends_on
#   3. Where is each part present?     -> parts.<id>.present_in
#
# If a change alters the shape of the repository (a part is added, removed,
# moved, renamed; a dependency edge appears or disappears; a part starts or
# stops shipping in an application), this file changes in the same commit.
# A change that leaves this file wrong is a broken change.

schema: repo-map/v1
updated: 2026-07-31

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Field reference — read once, applies to every entry below
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# applications:
#   <app_id>:
#     path        Directory the deployable lives in.
#     kind        What it is, so you can infer its build and run story.
#     summary     One line: who uses it, for what.
#
# parts:
#   <part_id>:
#     path        Root of the part. The part owns everything under here,
#                 plus the paths in `also_owns`, and nothing else.
#     summary     One line: what this part is responsible for.
#     depends_on  Part ids this part is allowed to import. Direct edges only;
#                 transitive dependencies are not repeated. [] means leaf.
#     present_in  Application ids whose build includes this part. This is the
#                 answer to "where does my change ship?".
#     api         The import specifier other parts must use. Reaching past it
#                 into internal files is a defect, in either direction.
#     read_first  Ordered, at most five files. Reading these is enough to make
#                 a small, correct change inside the part.
#     also_owns   Paths outside `path` (usually inside an application) that
#                 still belong to this part's slice.
#     notes       Optional. Anything about the part that would surprise you.
#
# Your slice = path + also_owns + the `api` and `read_first` files of each
# part in depends_on. Do not read the rest of the repository. If you believe
# you need to, that is a finding to report, not a thing to do.

applications:

  web:
    path: apps/web
    kind: next.js application, public internet
    summary: The customer-facing product.

  admin:
    path: apps/admin
    kind: vite single-page application, behind the VPN
    summary: Internal console used by support staff.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Worked example — dependency graph
#
#   billing ──▶ identity
#      │
#      └──────▶ ui
#
#   identity and ui are leaves. billing is present in `web` only.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

parts:

  ui:
    path: packages/ui
    summary: Design-system primitives — buttons, forms, layout, tokens. No product logic.
    depends_on: []
    present_in: [web, admin]
    api: "@acme/ui"
    read_first:
      - packages/ui/README.md
      - packages/ui/src/index.ts
      - packages/ui/src/tokens.css
    also_owns: []
    notes: >
      Present in both applications, so every change here is a change to both.
      Additive changes only unless the task explicitly says otherwise.

  identity:
    path: packages/identity
    summary: Accounts, sessions and permission checks. Owns the session cookie format.
    depends_on: []
    present_in: [web, admin]
    api: "@acme/identity"
    read_first:
      - packages/identity/README.md
      - packages/identity/src/index.ts
      - packages/identity/src/session.ts
      - packages/identity/src/permissions.ts
    also_owns:
      - "apps/web/app/(auth)/**"
      - "apps/admin/src/routes/login/**"
    notes: >
      The session cookie is read by both applications and by billing. Changing
      its shape is a coordinated change across every entry whose depends_on
      contains `identity` — do not attempt it inside a single-part task.

  billing:
    path: packages/billing
    summary: Plans, subscriptions, invoices and the Stripe webhook handler.
    depends_on: [identity, ui]
    present_in: [web]
    api: "@acme/billing"
    read_first:
      - packages/billing/README.md
      - packages/billing/src/index.ts
      - packages/billing/src/subscription.ts
      - packages/billing/src/webhook.ts
    also_owns:
      - "apps/web/app/settings/billing/**"
      - "apps/web/app/api/webhooks/stripe/**"
    notes: >
      Not present in admin. Support staff see billing state through a read-only
      endpoint served by web, not by importing this part. If a task asks admin
      to import billing, the first step is adding `admin` to present_in here
      and checking rule `presence-is-downward-closed` — then stop and report,
      because that is a repository-shape change, not a feature.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rules — these hold for every part, and CI enforces the mechanical ones
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

rules:

  - id: acyclic
    rule: >
      depends_on must form a directed acyclic graph. If you need a cycle, the
      shared thing wants to be its own part, or one of the two parts is too big.

  - id: presence-is-downward-closed
    rule: >
      If A depends_on B, then present_in(A) must be a subset of present_in(B).
      A part cannot depend on something absent from an application it ships in.
      Check this before adding an edge; it is the most common way this file goes
      wrong.

  - id: no-reverse-edges
    rule: >
      "Who depends on me" is deliberately not stored, so that each edge has one
      source of truth. To find your blast radius, search this file for your part
      id under depends_on.

  - id: api-only
    rule: >
      Imports that cross a part boundary go through that part's `api`. Deep
      imports into another part's internals are a defect even when they compile.

  - id: undeclared-is-out-of-scope
    rule: >
      If the work requires editing a path in no part's slice, or in another
      part's slice, stop and report it. Do not widen your own slice silently.

  - id: map-travels-with-the-change
    rule: >
      Adding, removing, moving or re-hosting a part updates this file in the
      same commit as the code.

checks:
  command: pnpm repo:map:check
  verifies:
    - every parts.<id>.path and also_owns glob matches at least one file
    - every id in depends_on and present_in exists
    - the depends_on graph is acyclic
    - rule presence-is-downward-closed holds for every edge
    - no file in the repository is claimed by two parts, or by none

how_to_use:
  - step: locate
    do: Find the one part your task belongs to. If it appears to be two, stop and report.
  - step: slice
    do: >
      Read that part's read_first files, then the `api` surface of each part in
      its depends_on. That is your whole reading list.
  - step: blast_radius
    do: >
      Before editing anything exported through `api`, list the parts whose
      depends_on names yours, and the union of their present_in. That union is
      what you can break.
  - step: finish
    do: >
      Re-read this entry. If your change made any field here untrue, fix the
      field. Report anything you found that this file does not describe.
```

I chose YAML because it is the only common format that carries comments, and most of this file's value is the field reference and rules that let an agent use it correctly without reading anything else first. The shape is a flat map keyed by part id rather than a nested tree, so an agent can jump to its own entry and the reverse-dependency lookup is a single search of one small file. I stored only forward edges (`depends_on`) and only presence (`present_in`), deriving "who uses me" and "what does this app contain" by scanning, because duplicated edges are the thing most likely to drift out of date. Every field is either something an agent acts on or something CI can verify, which is what keeps the file honest as the repository grows.

```yaml
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# repo-map.yaml — the root map of this monorepo.
#
# It answers three questions and deliberately nothing else:
#   1. What are the parts?            → parts[].id + parts[].does
#   2. What depends on what?          → parts[].depends_on
#   3. Where does each part ship?     → parts[].apps
#
# READING PROTOCOL (humans and coding agents)
# To work on part P, load exactly:
#   • this file
#   • every path in P.owns
#   • for each id in P.depends_on: only that part's `contract` files
# That is the whole slice. Nothing else in the repository should be opened.
# If the slice is not sufficient to do the work, then either the part
# boundary is wrong or this file is stale — fix one of those. Do not widen
# the read.
#
# RULES (checked by `validated_by`; CI fails on violation)
#   R1  depends_on must be acyclic.
#   R2  Code in part A may import from part B only through B.contract,
#       and only if B appears in A.depends_on.
#   R3  A part's `apps` must be a subset of every dependency's `apps`.
#       You cannot ship a part into an app where its dependency is absent.
#   R4  Every directory under apps/ and parts/ is claimed by exactly one
#       entry below. Unclaimed directories are a build error.
#   R5  One writer per part at a time. Before editing, an agent takes the
#       part's `owner` lane; concurrent agents must hold different lanes.
#
# App membership is declared once, on the part. Apps do not list their parts —
# a derived list would drift. To find an app's parts, filter parts[] by apps[].
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

schema: monorepo-map/v1
updated: 2026-07-31
validated_by: tools/check-repo-map.ts

apps:
  - id: web
    path: apps/web
    does: Customer-facing scheduling app (Next.js, deployed to Vercel).

  - id: console
    path: apps/console
    does: Internal support and administration app (Next.js, VPN-only).

  - id: jobs
    path: apps/jobs
    does: Scheduled and queued background workers (Node, deployed to Fly).

parts:
  - id: identity
    path: parts/identity
    does: >-
      Accounts, sessions, and the Actor object that every other part
      authorises against.
    owner: platform-lane
    owns:
      - parts/identity
    contract:
      - parts/identity/src/index.ts
      - parts/identity/src/types.ts
    depends_on: []
    apps: [web, console, jobs]

  - id: billing
    path: parts/billing
    does: >-
      Plans, subscriptions, invoices, and the Stripe webhook handler.
    owner: revenue-lane
    owns:
      - parts/billing
    contract:
      - parts/billing/src/index.ts
      - parts/billing/src/types.ts
    depends_on: [identity]
    apps: [web, console, jobs]
    notes: >-
      Present in jobs because nightly invoice generation runs there.
      Reads Actor from identity; never reads identity's tables directly.

  - id: audit-log
    path: parts/audit-log
    does: >-
      Append-only record of privileged actions, plus the viewer that
      renders it.
    owner: trust-lane
    owns:
      - parts/audit-log
    contract:
      - parts/audit-log/src/index.ts
    depends_on: [identity]
    apps: [console]
    notes: >-
      Console only. The log is written by the console's own mutations and
      is never exposed to customers, so web and jobs do not link it.
      By R3 this is legal: [console] is a subset of identity's apps.
```

I chose YAML because it is parsed reliably by every agent runtime yet still supports comments, and the reading protocol and boundary rules matter as much as the data — a JSON file could not carry them without a parallel README that would drift. The shape is a flat `parts` list rather than a nested tree so that an agent can find its entry with one scan and never has to reason about the whole structure. App membership lives on the part alone, giving each fact a single home and making R3 checkable by a short script. Field names (`owns`, `contract`, `depends_on`, `apps`) are chosen to state the constraint they impose, so an agent that reads only the field names still infers the correct behaviour.

```yaml
# repo-map.yaml — the one file every agent reads in full.
#
# Purpose: let an agent do a job in one part of this monorepo without reading the rest of it.
#
# Agent protocol:
#   1. Read this file. It is the whole map; nothing else at the root is required reading.
#   2. Find your part under `parts:`.
#   3. Read everything under your part's `path`.
#   4. For each id in your part's `depends_on`, read ONLY that part's `contract` file.
#      Do not open a dependency's `path`. If the contract does not answer your question,
#      that is a defect in the contract — report it rather than reading the implementation.
#   5. Change only files matching your part's `owns`. Everything else belongs to another
#      agent that may be editing it right now.
#   6. If you change a `contract`, add or drop a dependency, or add or drop a part from an
#      app, update this file in the same commit.
#
# Invariants (CI checks these; so should you before committing):
#   - every id in `depends_on` and `present_in` exists in `parts:` / `apps:`
#   - `depends_on` is acyclic
#   - if part A depends on part B, A.present_in is a subset of B.present_in
#   - `owns` globs of any two parts do not overlap
#   - reverse edges ("who uses me?") are derived from this file, never written down here

schema: repo-map/v1

apps:
  web:
    path: apps/web
    summary: Customer-facing Next.js app. Where end users sign in and pay.
  admin:
    path: apps/admin
    summary: Internal back-office. Staff only, behind the VPN.
  jobs:
    path: apps/jobs
    summary: Scheduled and queued background workers. No HTTP surface.

parts:

  identity:
    path: packages/identity
    contract: packages/identity/src/index.ts
    summary: >
      Accounts, sessions, and permission checks. Owns the users and sessions
      tables and is the only part permitted to read or write a password hash.
    depends_on: []
    present_in: [web, admin, jobs]
    owns:
      - packages/identity/**
      - db/migrations/*__identity_*.sql

  billing:
    path: packages/billing
    contract: packages/billing/src/index.ts
    summary: >
      Plans, subscriptions, invoices, and the Stripe webhook handler. Answers
      "may this account use this feature right now?" Owns the subscriptions
      and invoices tables.
    depends_on: [identity]      # must resolve an account before pricing anything
    present_in: [web, admin, jobs]
    owns:
      - packages/billing/**
      - db/migrations/*__billing_*.sql

  audit-log:
    path: packages/audit-log
    contract: packages/audit-log/src/index.ts
    summary: >
      Append-only record of staff actions, plus the viewer UI. Admin-only by
      design: customer-facing surfaces must never link to it.
    depends_on: [identity]      # every entry is attributed to a staff user
    present_in: [admin]         # deliberately absent from web and jobs
    owns:
      - packages/audit-log/**
      - db/migrations/*__audit_*.sql
```

I chose YAML because the reading protocol and the invariants are the load-bearing half of this file, and YAML lets those live as comments beside the data rather than in a separate document that agents would drift from — JSON would have forced them out. Parts and apps are keyed maps rather than lists so an agent can jump straight to its own entry by id, and so no id is ever written twice. The three questions map to exactly three fields per part — `path`, `depends_on`, `present_in` — with `contract` and `owns` added because they are what actually keep the slice small and keep concurrent agents off each other's files. It stays machine-parseable, so the invariants at the top are enforced in CI instead of being politely requested.

output:
```yaml
# repo-map.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The one file every agent reads first. It is the only place where the shape
# of this repository is written down; everything else is code.
#
# It answers exactly three questions:
#   1. What are the parts?            -> parts[].id / .path / .summary
#   2. What depends on what?          -> parts[].depends_on
#   3. Where does each part ship?     -> parts[].present_in
#
# If this file and the code disagree, this file is wrong: fix it in the same
# commit as the code.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

schema: repo-map/1
updated: 2026-07-31

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How to read this file if you are an agent
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent_protocol:
  # You are assigned one part id. That is your part.
  read_in_full:
    - this file
    - the `path` of your part
  read_interface_only:
    # For each id in your part's `depends_on` (transitively), read only its
    # `public_interface` file. Do not read the rest of that part's `path`.
    - depends_on -> public_interface
  do_not_read:
    - any part that is neither your part nor one of its dependencies
    - any application `path` your part is not `present_in`
  do_not_edit:
    - any `path` outside your own part
    # Need a change in another part? Do not reach in. Open a request in
    # docs/cross-part-requests/ naming both part ids, and keep working.
  before_you_finish:
    # New import from another part? New app? New part? Update this file too.
    - reconcile `depends_on` and `present_in` with what you actually wrote

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conventions that give the fields below a single meaning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
conventions:
  dependency_direction: >
    `depends_on` lists the parts that this part imports from. Arrows point from
    consumer to provider. Dependencies are direct only; transitive ones are
    derived, never listed.
  import_rule: >
    Code may only import a dependency through that dependency's
    `public_interface`. Deep imports into another part's internals are a bug.
  present_in_meaning: >
    The applications whose build graph contains this part. A part with two
    entries is genuinely shared: changing it changes both applications.
  path_meaning: >
    A single directory. A part is exactly its directory, tests included.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Applications: the things that get built, deployed and used
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
applications:
  - id: web
    path: apps/web
    summary: Customer-facing scheduling web app.
    build: pnpm --filter web build

  - id: mobile
    path: apps/mobile
    summary: React Native client for the same customers.
    build: pnpm --filter mobile build

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parts: the units of work. One agent per part.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
parts:
  - id: identity
    path: packages/identity
    summary: Sessions, tokens and the current-user object. No UI.
    public_interface: packages/identity/src/index.ts
    depends_on: []
    present_in: [web, mobile]

  - id: booking
    path: packages/booking
    summary: Availability rules, booking creation, cancellation and rescheduling.
    public_interface: packages/booking/src/index.ts
    depends_on: [identity]        # reads the current user to authorise a booking
    present_in: [web, mobile]

  - id: reports
    path: packages/reports
    summary: Aggregates bookings into the operator dashboard tables and CSV export.
    public_interface: packages/reports/src/index.ts
    depends_on: [booking]
    present_in: [web]             # dashboard is web-only; not built into mobile

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariants. CI checks these; they are also what makes a slice safe to read.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
invariants:
  - Every id in `depends_on` is a declared part id.
  - Every id in `present_in` is a declared application id.
  - The `depends_on` graph is acyclic.
  - A dependency's `present_in` must cover its consumer's `present_in`.
    # e.g. `reports` is in [web], so `booking` must include web. It does.
    # Adding `reports` to mobile would therefore be legal; adding a web-only
    # dependency to `booking` would not, because `booking` also ships on mobile.
  - Every part has a `public_interface` file that exists.
  - Every `path` and application `path` exists and no two overlap.
  - Every directory under packages/ and apps/ appears here exactly once.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Adding to this file
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
maintenance:
  new_part: >
    Add the entry before writing the code, so parallel agents see it. Choose the
    smallest `present_in` that is true today.
  new_dependency: >
    Add the id to `depends_on`, then re-check the coverage invariant. If it
    fails, the shared logic belongs in a new part rather than in the dependency.
  removing_an_application_from_present_in: >
    A narrowing change. Grep for the part inside that application's `path`
    first; the invariant checker will not catch dead imports for you.
```

I chose YAML because this file has two audiences at once — a checker that must enforce the invariants and an agent that must decide what *not* to read — and YAML is the only common format that parses cleanly while still carrying the comments that explain the reading protocol. Dependencies live on each part rather than in a separate graph section, so an agent handed a single part id finds its whole slice in one entry and nothing is stated twice. Application membership is a list of ids on the part, not a list of parts on the app, for the same reason: one lookup per agent, and the coverage invariant becomes a local check. I kept it declarative and free of build details so the file stays a map rather than drifting into a second, weaker copy of the build configuration.

```toml
# repo-map.toml
#
# The only file every agent reads in full. It answers three questions and nothing else:
#
#   1. What are the parts?        -> the [[part]] blocks
#   2. What depends on what?      -> part.depends_on
#   3. Where does each part ship? -> part.apps
#
# READING PROTOCOL for an agent assigned to part <id>:
#   1. read [repo] and the one [[part]] block whose id = <id>
#   2. read that block's `read_first` files, in order
#   3. for each id in its `depends_on`, read only that part's `entry` file
#   4. read nothing else; if that is not enough context, this map is wrong --
#      fix the map in its own commit before touching code
#
# INVARIANTS (CI enforces these; keep them true):
#   I1  part ids are unique, lowercase, kebab-case, and outlive any path rename
#   I2  depends_on holds part ids only, and the graph is acyclic
#   I3  a part may import another part only through that part's `entry`
#   I4  if A depends on B, then A.apps is a subset of B.apps
#   I5  apps holds app ids only; a part with apps = [] is dead, delete it
#   I6  app -> parts is derived from part.apps and is never written down here
#   I7  package.json / build config is the mechanical truth; CI diffs it against
#       this file and fails on disagreement, so this map cannot quietly rot
#   I8  a change to the structure described here lands in the same commit

schema_version = 1
kind = "repo-map"

[repo]
name = "acme"
purpose = "Subscription product: a customer-facing web app and an internal admin console."
package_manager = "pnpm"
map_owner = "@platform"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Applications: the deployable units. Each part below declares which of these
# it is present in.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[app]]
id = "web"
name = "Customer web app"
path = "apps/web"
entry = "apps/web/src/main.tsx"
deploys_to = "web.acme.com"

[[app]]
id = "admin"
name = "Internal admin console"
path = "apps/admin"
entry = "apps/admin/src/main.tsx"
deploys_to = "admin.acme.internal"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parts: the units of work. One agent per part.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[part]]
id = "identity"
name = "Identity"
path = "packages/identity"
purpose = "Accounts, sessions, and the permission check every other part calls."
entry = "packages/identity/src/index.ts"
read_first = [
  "packages/identity/README.md",
  "packages/identity/src/index.ts",
  "packages/identity/src/permissions.ts",
]
depends_on = []
apps = ["web", "admin"]
verify = "pnpm --filter @acme/identity test"
notes = "Root of the graph. Widening `entry` is a repo-wide change: propose it in the map first."

[[part]]
id = "billing"
name = "Billing"
path = "packages/billing"
purpose = "Plans, subscriptions, invoices, and the payment-provider webhook handler."
entry = "packages/billing/src/index.ts"
read_first = [
  "packages/billing/README.md",
  "packages/billing/src/index.ts",
  "packages/billing/src/subscription.ts",
]
depends_on = ["identity"]
apps = ["web", "admin"]
verify = "pnpm --filter @acme/billing test"
notes = "Gets the current actor from identity's `entry`. Never reads the users table directly."

[[part]]
id = "support-inbox"
name = "Support inbox"
path = "packages/support-inbox"
purpose = "Ticket queue and reply composer used by support staff."
entry = "packages/support-inbox/src/index.ts"
read_first = [
  "packages/support-inbox/README.md",
  "packages/support-inbox/src/index.ts",
  "packages/support-inbox/src/queue.ts",
]
depends_on = ["identity"]
apps = ["admin"]
verify = "pnpm --filter @acme/support-inbox test"
notes = """
Admin-only, and allowed to be: I4 holds because ["admin"] is a subset of identity.apps.
Importing this from apps/web is a build error, not a review comment.
"""
```

I chose TOML because its array-of-tables syntax gives each part one flat, self-contained block that an agent can locate with a single grep and read in isolation — the same slicing property the repository itself is meant to have. It supports comments, so the reading protocol and the invariants live next to the data they govern rather than in a separate document that drifts. It has no significant whitespace and no ambiguous scalars, so an agent appending or rewriting a block cannot silently corrupt the structure or the values the way it can in YAML. And the schema keeps one direction of truth — parts declare their dependencies and their applications, while the application-to-parts view is derived — so there is never a second place that has to be updated in step.

```yaml
# Single source of truth for how this monorepo is organized.
```
